subject: Materials Science
title: 3D Printing with Polymers
description: A fast breakdown of 3D Printing with Polymers for builders.

hook.text: No mold. No die. Just a nozzle, a spool of filament, and a digital file.

buildup.text: FDM printers melt polymer filament and deposit it layer by layer into 3D objects.

discovery.text: PLA, ABS, PETG, and nylon are all printable — each chosen for different properties.

twist.text: Printed parts are weaker along layer lines — anisotropy is the Achilles heel of 3D printing.

climax.text: Surgeons now 3D-print patient-specific implants from biocompatible polymers before surgery.

punchline.text: 3D printing trades speed for freedom of shape.

quiz.question: What is a key weakness of 3D-printed polymer parts?
options: They are weaker along layer lines
They cannot be made from recycled material
